newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds remain bid after roll over.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds remain bid after roll over.

text.p: *Australian bonds finish firmer on day where activity was dominated by rollover of expiring December futures contracts.
*Although local market well bid on the day, offshore expected to provide leads in pre-Christmas trading.
Australian bonds managed to hold a bid tone through a day dominated by the rollover of the December futures contracts, traders said.

With the U.S. market finishing last week firmer and then remaining firm in Tokyo trade, and the rollover being fairly orderly, traders said the bid tone led to some outright buying and kept bonds supported in the afternoon session.
However, volumes were lower through the afternoon session, as focus turned to the U.S. market, and Tuesday's meeting of the policy setting FOMC, which should guide the local market into year-end.
"The focus into Christmas is on the U.S. with fresh supply due this week and the FOMC meeting tomorrow night," one trader said.
Partial indicators of inflation released today showed declining import and export prices in October, and a small rise in manufacturing input prices, but had little market impact.
The only local data seen as having the potential to shift the markets ahead of Christmas is Wednesday's merchandise imports data for November.
The data, a forerunner to the current account deficit, is expected to show a 1.0 percent rise in the month.

The stronger showing of the local bond market saw spreads narrow across the board, with the long end leading the way. The spread to U.S. 10 years moved back towards 100 points, while New Zealand market is waiting on Tuesday's Reserve Bank six-monthly monetary policy statement.
